# Hypertension

## Definition
Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure.

## Classification
| Category | Systolic (mmHg) | Diastolic (mmHg) |
|----------|----------------|------------------|
| Normal | <120 | <80 |
| Elevated | 120-129 | <80 |
| Stage 1 HTN | 130-139 | 80-89 |
| Stage 2 HTN | ≥140 | ≥90 |
| Crisis | >180 | >120 |

## First-Line Treatment
- Lifestyle modification (DASH diet, reduce sodium, exercise)
- ACE inhibitors or ARBs for most patients
- Calcium channel blockers as alternative

See also: [Atenolol](../drugs/atenolol.md), [Amlodipine](../drugs/amlodipine.md)

## Monitoring
- BP check at every visit
- Home BP monitoring recommended
- Annual kidney function, electrolytes

# Diet for Diabetes

## Key Principles
- Reduce refined carbohydrates and sugars
- Include high-fiber foods (whole grains, legumes, vegetables)
- Limit saturated fats; prefer unsaturated fats
- Control portion sizes
- Regular meal timing (avoid skipping meals)

- Include dal, rajma, chana for protein
- Limit sweets, fried snacks, and sugary beverages
- 2-3 servings of fresh fruits daily (avoid fruit juices)

# Hypoglycemia Emergency

## Recognition
- Blood glucose <70 mg/dL
- Symptoms: trembling, sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger
- Severe: seizures, loss of consciousness

## Immediate Action
1. If conscious: Give 15-20g fast-acting glucose (3-4 glucose tablets, half cup juice, 1 tablespoon sugar in water)
2. Wait 15 minutes, recheck glucose
3. If still <70 mg/dL: repeat step 1
4. Once normalized: eat a snack with protein (biscuits with peanut butter)

## When to Call Emergency (112)
- Patient is unconscious
- Patient cannot swallow
- Glucose remains <50 mg/dL after 2 treatments
- Seizure activity

## Prevention
- Regular meal timing — do not skip meals
- Monitor glucose before and after exercise
- Carry glucose tablets or sugar sachets at all times
- Educate family members on recognizing symptoms

# Hypoglycemia Emergency

## Recognition
- Blood glucose <70 mg/dL
- Symptoms: trembling, sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger
- Severe: seizures, loss of consciousness

## Immediate Action
1. If conscious: Give 15-20g fast-acting glucose (3-4 glucose tablets, half cup juice, 1 tablespoon sugar in water)
2. Wait 15 minutes, recheck glucose
3. If still <70 mg/dL: repeat step 1
4. Once normalized: eat a snack with protein (biscuits with peanut butter)

## When to Call Emergency (112)
- Patient is unconscious
- Patient cannot swallow
- Glucose remains <50 mg/dL after 2 treatments
- Seizure activity

## Prevention
- Regular meal timing — do not skip meals
- Monitor glucose before and after exercise
- Carry glucose tablets or sugar sachets at all times
- Educate family members on recognizing symptoms

# Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)

## Class & Mechanism
Analgesic and antipyretic. Centrally inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and modulates the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center to reduce fever and alleviate mild-to-moderate pain.

## Clinical Indications & Physician Role
- First-line choice for symptomatic relief of fever, headache, body ache, and osteoarthritis.
- Your doctor may consider paracetamol spaced at intervals of at least 4 to 6 hours, adhering strictly to safe daily limits based on body weight and liver function.

## Critical Warnings: Liver Toxicity & Alcohol Interaction
- **Hepatotoxicity Warning**: Overdose depletes hepatic glutathione, causing toxic NAPQI metabolite accumulation and fatal acute hepatic necrosis.
- **Strictly Avoid with Alcohol**: Combining alcohol with paracetamol significantly elevates liver injury risk and reduces toxic clearance thresholds.
- **Hidden OTC Combinations**: Avoid concurrent cold syrups, sinus sachets, or headache balms containing undisclosed paracetamol.

## Toxicity Severity Classification
| Phase | Time Elapsed | Clinical Signs | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stage 1 | 0-24 hours | Nausea, vomiting, pallor, malaise, sweating | Emergency hospital referral; evaluate N-acetylcysteine |
| Stage 2 | 24-72 hours | Right upper quadrant abdominal pain, rising AST/ALT | Inpatient monitoring and liver protection |

# Hydration & Fluid Balance

## Baseline Requirements
ICMR 2023 guidelines recommend 2.5 to 3.5 liters of safe fluid intake daily for adults under average Indian climatic conditions. Fluid needs must be individualized: for conditions like heart failure or chronic kidney disease, your doctor may consider strict fluid and sodium restrictions.

## Indian Summer Heat & Electrolyte Depletion
During intense heatwaves (May–June) when daytime temperatures surpass 42°C–46°C, profuse sweating strips water and sodium, triggering heat exhaustion, hemoconcentration, and prerenal acute kidney injury.

## Definition
Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure.

## Classification
| Category | Systolic (mmHg) | Diastolic (mmHg) |
|----------|----------------|------------------|
| Normal | <120 | <80 |
| Elevated | 120-129 | <80 |
| Stage 1 HTN | 130-139 | 80-89 |
| Stage 2 HTN | ≥140 | ≥90 |
| Crisis | >180 | >120 |

## First-Line Treatment
- Lifestyle modification (DASH diet, reduce sodium, exercise)
- ACE inhibitors or ARBs for most patients
- Calcium channel blockers as alternative

See also: [Atenolol](../drugs/atenolol.md), [Amlodipine](../drugs/amlodipine.md)

- BP check at every visit
- Home BP monitoring recommended

# Exercise Guidelines — ICMR Recommendations

## General Indian Adult Recommendations
- **Minimum**: 150 minutes moderate-intensity activity per week (ICMR 2023)
- **Optimal**: 300 minutes/week for additional health benefits
- **Strength training**: 2 sessions/week for all adults ≥18

## Exercise by Health Condition

### Diabetes
- 30 minutes brisk walking DAILY — most effective single intervention
- Blood sugar: Check before exercise; postpone if <80 mg/dL or >250 mg/dL
- Best time: 1-2 hours after a meal (stabilizes post-meal sugar spike)
- Carry glucose biscuits/sweets in case of hypoglycemia during exercise

### Hypertension
- Aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, cycling): 30-45 min/day, 5 days/week
- **Avoid**: Heavy weight lifting, straining (raises BP acutely)
- Target HR during exercise: 50-70% of maximum (max HR = 220 - age)
- Start slow if newly diagnosed; build intensity over 4-6 weeks

### Heart Disease (post-event)
- Only after cardiologist clearance
- Begin with 10-min walks, gradually increase
- Stop if: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, dizziness

### Obesity (BMI > 27.5 for Indians)
- Start with low-impact: walking, swimming, cycling
- 60 min/day recommended for weight loss
- Indian millets (jowar, bajra, ragi) + exercise combination most effective

# Aspirin (Low-Dose)

## Class & Mechanism
Antiplatelet agent (acetylsalicylic acid). Irreversibly acetylates platelet cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1), blocking thromboxane A2 synthesis and preventing platelet aggregation and arterial thrombosis.

## Indications & Physician Considerations
- Secondary prevention of myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and in patients with coronary stents or bypass grafts.
- Your doctor may consider low-dose aspirin therapy after weighing individual ischemic benefit against gastrointestinal bleeding risk.

## Critical Warning: NOT for Self-Medication
- **Do not self-prescribe aspirin**: Routine self-medication as a "heart tonic" or preventive pill without a physician's directive is dangerous.
- In primary prevention (without established cardiovascular disease), bleeding risks often outweigh benefits under ICMR guidelines.

Heatstroke is an acute medical emergency occurring when thermoregulation fails and core body temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F), accompanied by central nervous system (CNS) dysfunction and multi-organ failure.

# Exercise Guidelines — ICMR Recommendations

## General Indian Adult Recommendations
- **Minimum**: 150 minutes moderate-intensity activity per week (ICMR 2023)
- **Optimal**: 300 minutes/week for additional health benefits
- **Strength training**: 2 sessions/week for all adults ≥18

- Carry glucose biscuits/sweets in case of hypoglycemia during exercise

### Hypertension
- Aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, cycling): 30-45 min/day, 5 days/week
- **Avoid**: Heavy weight lifting, straining (raises BP acutely)

- Start slow if newly diagnosed; build intensity over 4-6 weeks

- Only after cardiologist clearance
- Begin with 10-min walks, gradually increase
- Stop if: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, dizziness

- Start with low-impact: walking, swimming, cycling

# Tobacco & Smoking Cessation

## Burden & ICMR Statistics
Tobacco consumption is the single most preventable cause of death in India, responsible for over 1.35 million deaths annually (ICMR-NCDIR 2023). Tobacco use drastically accelerates endothelial damage, precipitating premature heart attacks, strokes, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and oral and lung cancers.

## Forms of Tobacco Prevalent in India
| Tobacco Form | Composition & Usage | Specific Health Hazards |
|---|---|---|
| **Bidi** | Sun-cured tobacco flake rolled in tendu leaf | Delivers 3x more nicotine and 5x more carbon monoxide than manufactured cigarettes |
| **Cigarettes** | Cured tobacco paper-wrapped | Accelerated coronary atherosclerosis, arterial stiffening, and [Hypertension](../conditions/hypertension.md) |

# Exercise Guidelines — ICMR Recommendations

## General Indian Adult Recommendations
- **Minimum**: 150 minutes moderate-intensity activity per week (ICMR 2023)
- **Optimal**: 300 minutes/week for additional health benefits
- **Strength training**: 2 sessions/week for all adults ≥18

### Diabetes
- 30 minutes brisk walking DAILY — most effective single intervention

- Carry glucose biscuits/sweets in case of hypoglycemia during exercise

### Hypertension
- Aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, cycling): 30-45 min/day, 5 days/week
- **Avoid**: Heavy weight lifting, straining (raises BP acutely)

- Only after cardiologist clearance

- Stop if: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, dizziness

- Symptoms: trembling, sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger
- Severe: seizures, loss of consciousness

# Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)

## Class & Mechanism
Analgesic and antipyretic. Centrally inhibits prostaglandin synthesis and modulates the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center to reduce fever and alleviate mild-to-moderate pain.

# Amlodipine

## Class & Mechanism
Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (CCB). Inhibits calcium influx into vascular smooth muscle, promoting peripheral arterial vasodilation and reducing systemic blood pressure.

## Indications & Physician Role
- First-line monotherapy or combination therapy for essential [Hypertension](../conditions/hypertension.md) and chronic stable angina.
- Your doctor may consider amlodipine as a once-daily regimen, adjusting treatment based on BP targets and cardiovascular risk profile.

## Adverse Effect Severity Classification
| Severity | Manifestations | Action Required |
|---|---|---|
| Mild / Common | Peripheral pedal edema (ankle swelling), flushing, headache | Report at routine follow-up; evaluate salt intake |
| Moderate | Persistent dizziness, postural hypotension, palpitations | Doctor may consider dose modification or combination agent |
| Severe / Rare | Severe hypotension, syncope, generalized allergic reaction | Discontinue under guidance; urgent medical evaluation |

Acute chest discomfort often indicates Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) or ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI).

# Amlodipine

## Class & Mechanism
Long-acting dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (CCB). Inhibits calcium influx into vascular smooth muscle, promoting peripheral arterial vasodilation and reducing systemic blood pressure.

## Indications & Physician Role
- First-line monotherapy or combination therapy for essential [Hypertension](../conditions/hypertension.md) and chronic stable angina.
- Your doctor may consider amlodipine as a once-daily regimen, adjusting treatment based on BP targets and cardiovascular risk profile.

## Adverse Effect Severity Classification
| Severity | Manifestations | Action Required |
|---|---|---|
| Mild / Common | Peripheral pedal edema (ankle swelling), flushing, headache | Report at routine follow-up; evaluate salt intake |
| Moderate | Persistent dizziness, postural hypotension, palpitations | Doctor may consider dose modification or combination agent |
| Severe / Rare | Severe hypotension, syncope, generalized allergic reaction | Discontinue under guidance; urgent medical evaluation |

## India-Specific Clinical Context
- **Pedal Edema Misconception**: Ankle swelling is common in warm Indian climates and prolonged standing; patients frequently mistake this for kidney failure. Clinical reassurance and review are vital.
- **High Sodium Intake**: Traditional Indian diets rich in pickles (achaar), papad, and namkeen blunt CCB efficacy.

# Hypoglycemia Emergency

## Recognition
- Blood glucose <70 mg/dL
- Symptoms: trembling, sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger
- Severe: seizures, loss of consciousness

## Immediate Action
1. If conscious: Give 15-20g fast-acting glucose (3-4 glucose tablets, half cup juice, 1 tablespoon sugar in water)
2. Wait 15 minutes, recheck glucose
3. If still <70 mg/dL: repeat step 1
4. Once normalized: eat a snack with protein (biscuits with peanut butter)

## When to Call Emergency (112)
- Patient is unconscious
- Patient cannot swallow
- Glucose remains <50 mg/dL after 2 treatments
- Seizure activity

## Prevention
- Regular meal timing — do not skip meals
- Monitor glucose before and after exercise
- Carry glucose tablets or sugar sachets at all times
- Educate family members on recognizing symptoms

- Include high-fiber foods (whole grains, legumes, vegetables)

- Control portion sizes
- Regular meal timing (avoid skipping meals)

Namaste! It is very good that you are being proactive about your health during the monsoon. Waterlogging near your home creates a perfect environment for certain diseases to spread. Based on ICMR guidelines, here are the main conditions you should watch out for, along with how to recognize them:

### 1. Vector-Borne Diseases (Mosquito-Borne)
Stagnant water from waterlogging is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, particularly *Aedes* (for Dengue/Chikungunya) and *Anopheles* (for Malaria). [Doc 1]

*   **Dengue Fever:**
    *   **Watch for:** Sudden high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes (retro-orbital pain), and severe muscle/joint pain (often called "breakbone fever"). [Doc 1, Doc 2]
    *   **Warning Signs:** If you notice abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or any bleeding from gums/nose, seek medical help immediately. [Doc 2]
*   **Malaria:**
    *   **Watch for:** Cycles of shaking chills, high fever, and drenching sweats. [Doc 1]
    *   **Note:** If you experience confusion or altered consciousness along with fever, it is a medical emergency. [Doc 1]
*   **Chikungunya:**
    *   **Watch for:** High fever accompanied by severe, debilitating joint pain. [Doc 1]

### 2. Water-Borne Diseases
Contact with floodwater or consuming contaminated water/food can lead to these infections. [Doc 1]

*   **Leptospirosis:**
    *   **Watch for:** Severe tenderness in the calf muscles, redness in the eyes (conjunctival suffusion), and high fever. [Doc 1]
    *   **Warning Signs:** Jaundice (yellowing of eyes/skin) or reduced urine output are serious indicators. [Doc 1]
*   **Typhoid & Acute Gastroenteritis:**
    *   **Watch for:** Step-ladder fever (fever that rises gradually), abdominal pain, and diarrhea. [Doc 1]
    *   **Hydration:** If you have diarrhea or vomiting, it is crucial to prevent dehydration. Use WHO ORS, tender coconut water (*nariyal pani*), or light moong dal soup. [Doc 2]
*   **Hepatitis A/E:**
    *   **Watch for:** Jaundice, fatigue, and abdominal discomfort after exposure to contaminated water. [Doc 1]

### 🛡️ Prevention Tips for Your Home
1.  **Eliminate Breeding Sites:** Check coolers, discarded plastic containers, flower vases, and overhead tanks for stagnant water. Empty or cover them. [Doc 2]
2.  **Protect Yourself:** Wear rubber boots or shoes when walking through waterlogged areas to prevent skin contact with contaminated water (Leptospirosis risk). [Doc 1]
3.  **Safe Water:** Drink only boiled or properly filtered water. Avoid street food during heavy rains.
4.  **Hydration:** Keep your family well-hydrated with safe fluids like *nariyal pani* or ORS if anyone feels unwell. [Doc 2]

### 🚨 When to Seek Immediate Medical Help
Please consult a doctor immediately if you or a family member experiences:
*   Persistent vomiting or severe abdominal pain.
*   Bleeding from gums, nose, or blood in vomit/stool.
*   Jaundice (yellow eyes/skin) or dark urine.
*   Confusion, drowsiness, or difficulty breathing.
*   **Chest pain, severe breathlessness, or unconsciousness: 🚨 CALL 112 NOW. Do not wait.**

Stay safe and keep your surroundings clean!

⚕️ I am an AI health assistant, not a doctor.

# Diet for Diabetes

## Key Principles
- Reduce refined carbohydrates and sugars
- Include high-fiber foods (whole grains, legumes, vegetables)
- Limit saturated fats; prefer unsaturated fats
- Control portion sizes
- Regular meal timing (avoid skipping meals)

## Indian Diet Specific
- Replace white rice with brown rice or millets (jowar, bajra, ragi)
- Use mustard oil or groundnut oil instead of palm oil
- Include dal, rajma, chana for protein
- Limit sweets, fried snacks, and sugary beverages
- 2-3 servings of fresh fruits daily (avoid fruit juices)

## Recognition
- Blood glucose <70 mg/dL
- Symptoms: trembling, sweating, confusion, dizziness, hunger
- Severe: seizures, loss of consciousness

## Immediate Action
1. If conscious: Give 15-20g fast-acting glucose (3-4 glucose tablets, half cup juice, 1 tablespoon sugar in water)

3. If still <70 mg/dL: repeat step 1
4. Once normalized: eat a snack with protein (biscuits with peanut butter)

- Patient is unconscious
- Patient cannot swallow
- Glucose remains <50 mg/dL after 2 treatments
- Seizure activity

- Regular meal timing — do not skip meals

- Carry glucose tablets or sugar sachets at all times

## Baseline Requirements
ICMR 2023 guidelines recommend 2.5 to 3.5 liters of safe fluid intake daily for adults under average Indian climatic conditions. Fluid needs must be individualized: for conditions like heart failure or chronic kidney disease, your doctor may consider strict fluid and sodium restrictions.

## Overview & Recognition
Heatstroke is an acute medical emergency occurring when thermoregulation fails and core body temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F), accompanied by central nervous system (CNS) dysfunction and multi-organ failure.

# Exercise Guidelines — ICMR Recommendations

## General Indian Adult Recommendations
- **Minimum**: 150 minutes moderate-intensity activity per week (ICMR 2023)
- **Optimal**: 300 minutes/week for additional health benefits
- **Strength training**: 2 sessions/week for all adults ≥18

## Exercise by Health Condition

### Diabetes
- 30 minutes brisk walking DAILY — most effective single intervention
- Blood sugar: Check before exercise; postpone if <80 mg/dL or >250 mg/dL
- Best time: 1-2 hours after a meal (stabilizes post-meal sugar spike)
- Carry glucose biscuits/sweets in case of hypoglycemia during exercise

### Hypertension
- Aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, cycling): 30-45 min/day, 5 days/week
- **Avoid**: Heavy weight lifting, straining (raises BP acutely)
- Target HR during exercise: 50-70% of maximum (max HR = 220 - age)
- Start slow if newly diagnosed; build intensity over 4-6 weeks

### Heart Disease (post-event)
- Only after cardiologist clearance
- Begin with 10-min walks, gradually increase
- Stop if: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, dizziness

### Obesity (BMI > 27.5 for Indians)
- Start with low-impact: walking, swimming, cycling
- 60 min/day recommended for weight loss
- Indian millets (jowar, bajra, ragi) + exercise combination most effective

# Hypertension

## Definition
Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure.

## Classification
| Category | Systolic (mmHg) | Diastolic (mmHg) |
|----------|----------------|------------------|
| Normal | <120 | <80 |
| Elevated | 120-129 | <80 |
| Stage 1 HTN | 130-139 | 80-89 |
| Stage 2 HTN | ≥140 | ≥90 |
| Crisis | >180 | >120 |

## First-Line Treatment
- Lifestyle modification (DASH diet, reduce sodium, exercise)
- ACE inhibitors or ARBs for most patients
- Calcium channel blockers as alternative

See also: [Atenolol](../drugs/atenolol.md), [Amlodipine](../drugs/amlodipine.md)

## Monitoring
- BP check at every visit
- Home BP monitoring recommended
- Annual kidney function, electrolytes

# Exercise Guidelines — ICMR Recommendations

## General Indian Adult Recommendations
- **Minimum**: 150 minutes moderate-intensity activity per week (ICMR 2023)
- **Optimal**: 300 minutes/week for additional health benefits
- **Strength training**: 2 sessions/week for all adults ≥18

## Exercise by Health Condition

### Diabetes
- 30 minutes brisk walking DAILY — most effective single intervention
- Blood sugar: Check before exercise; postpone if <80 mg/dL or >250 mg/dL
- Best time: 1-2 hours after a meal (stabilizes post-meal sugar spike)
- Carry glucose biscuits/sweets in case of hypoglycemia during exercise

### Hypertension
- Aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, cycling): 30-45 min/day, 5 days/week
- **Avoid**: Heavy weight lifting, straining (raises BP acutely)
- Target HR during exercise: 50-70% of maximum (max HR = 220 - age)
- Start slow if newly diagnosed; build intensity over 4-6 weeks

### Heart Disease (post-event)
- Only after cardiologist clearance
- Begin with 10-min walks, gradually increase
- Stop if: chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, dizziness

### Obesity (BMI > 27.5 for Indians)
- Start with low-impact: walking, swimming, cycling
- 60 min/day recommended for weight loss
- Indian millets (jowar, bajra, ragi) + exercise combination most effective

# Heatstroke Emergency Protocol

## Overview & Recognition
Heatstroke is an acute medical emergency occurring when thermoregulation fails and core body temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F), accompanied by central nervous system (CNS) dysfunction and multi-organ failure.

## Diagnostic Criteria & Differential Triage
| Parameter | Heat Exhaustion | Heatstroke (Life-Threatening) |
|---|---|---|
| Core Body Temp | 38°C - 40°C (100.4°F - 104°F) | >40°C (>104°F) rectally / core |
| CNS Dysfunction | Intact or mild dizziness/fatigue | Confusion, delirium, seizures, stupor, coma |
| Skin / Sweating | Profuse sweating, pale, cool | Dry/hot skin (classic) or sweating (exertional) |
| Systemic Impact | Mild dehydration, hemoconcentration | Rhabdomyolysis, renal failure, DIC, shock |

## Severity Classification
- **Mild Heat Illness**: Heat rash (prickly heat/miliaria), heat cramps in calf/abdominal muscles, heat edema.
- **Heat Exhaustion**: Tachycardia, dizziness, headache, intense thirst, nausea; mentation remains intact.
- **Heatstroke**: Core temp >40°C with altered sensorium, ataxia, seizures, or cardiovascular collapse.

# Hydration & Fluid Balance

## Baseline Requirements
ICMR 2023 guidelines recommend 2.5 to 3.5 liters of safe fluid intake daily for adults under average Indian climatic conditions. Fluid needs must be individualized: for conditions like heart failure or chronic kidney disease, your doctor may consider strict fluid and sodium restrictions.

## Indian Summer Heat & Electrolyte Depletion
During intense heatwaves (May–June) when daytime temperatures surpass 42°C–46°C, profuse sweating strips water and sodium, triggering heat exhaustion, hemoconcentration, and prerenal acute kidney injury.

## Rehydration Solutions & Electrolytes
| Rehydration Choice | Composition & Properties | Clinical Utility |
|---|---|---|
| **WHO-Formula ORS** | Exact sodium-glucose balance (75 mmol/L Na, 75 mmol/L glucose) | Gold standard for clinical dehydration, heat exhaustion, and acute diarrheal loss |
| **Traditional Chaas** | Diluted curd/buttermilk with roasted cumin (*jeera*) and curry leaves | Cooling probiotic electrolyte drink; replenishes potassium and minerals |
| **Nimbu Pani & Coconut Water** | Lemon water with a pinch of salt; tender coconut water | Natural potassium-rich hydration; avoid adding refined sugar for diabetics |

# Heat Health and Heatwave Management

## Overview & Indian Heatwave Criteria
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and NDMA define heatwaves based on departure from normal maximum temperatures:
- **Plains**: Max temperature ≥40°C (or departure ≥4.5°C above normal).
- **Hills & Coastal Areas**: Max temperature ≥30°C in hills, ≥37°C in coastal stations.
- **Severe Heatwave**: Departure ≥6.4°C or absolute maximum temperature ≥47°C.

## IMD Heat Alert Protocol & Public Actions
| Alert Level | Temperature Condition | Recommended Public Health Action |
|---|---|---|
| Green (Normal) | Normal summer range | Maintain baseline hydration; normal outdoor routine |
| Yellow (Watch) | Heatwave lasting 1-2 days | High-risk groups limit midday sun exposure (12 PM - 3 PM) |
| Orange (Alert) | Persistent heatwave 3-4 days | Reschedule outdoor work; ensure cool rest areas and ORS |
| Red (Warning) | Extreme heatwave >4 days | Suspend outdoor heavy physical labor; emergency cooling centers |

- **Moderate Strain (Heat Exhaustion)**: Dizziness, profuse sweating, nausea, tachycardia, preserved cognition.
